title: endpoint shapes for the extracted relation types
description: The node each relation type may run between, as one table both the report and the spec are read against. A relation outside its shape is COUNTED and REPORTED, never dropped: the shapes describe what the corpus actually says, and the first production merge found 756 relations outside the narrower reading of §2.4 — mostly a `Feature` motivating a `Problem`, which is a real sentence a KIP writes. Losing those would lose the answer to "why was this built". A descriptor is either a node label (`Document`, `WorkItem`, `Commit`, `Component`) or `Entity:<kind>`; an empty list means "any".
amended: 2026-09-07 — planner ruling after the first production merge; §2.4 amended to match.

DECIDES.note: The KIP page, or the issue that records the choice, decides.

MOTIVATED_BY.note: A KIP as often motivates the capability it adds as the choice it made.

REJECTS.note: A `Rejected Alternatives` section usually lists what was turned down without restating the decision, so the document itself is the rejecter.

IMPLEMENTS.note: What realises a capability: an issue, the commit that closed it, or the KIP that specifies it.

DEPENDS_ON.note: The widest shape on purpose: a dependency is stated between whatever two things the sentence names, and a KIP depending on another KIP is a Document on the target side.

INTRODUCES_RISK.note: Something the text states brings the risk. The source list was empty before 2026-09-07, which silently exempted this type from the check.
